event_triggers.E1: v0.6.0 event, unchanged: after observing step u, residual (mean of the last W=8 surprises, 12 d.p.) > tau x 0.5, or a window-tier event (as brute/driftsound._note_event)
event_triggers.E2: falsified certificate: the forecast for the taken action at step u carried a conditional certificate c and the observation at u is incompatible with c (bit c not in the observation mask). Constant-free.
event_triggers.E3: single-step surprise: s_u = -ln compatible_mass(published probabilities for u, observation u) > tau (tau6 for 2x2, tau7 for breadth; the frozen ALARM threshold applied to one step instead of the window mean). No new constant. Exact: tau6 = 1.645215 > ln 4 = 1.386294 and tau7 = 2.07944154168 > ln 8 = 2.07944154167984 (margin ~2e-13), so a forecast spread uniformly over all codes never triggers E3; E3 needs the realised observation to have had probability < e^-tau (0.1930 for 2x2, 0.1250 for 8 codes).
event_triggers.note: Inferred: when the published forecast is a certified one, E2 implies E3 (the falsified code carried >= 1-3eps/4 mass, so the compatible mass is <= 3 x eps/4 = 0.015, s >= 4.2 > tau6); E2 is kept as an explicit, constant-free trigger and each event records which triggers fired. Alarms (F4 RESIDUAL_SURPRISE), resume, probabilities and LU-R are NOT changed by E2/E3.

jump_window_definition.region: JumpWindowRegionK(n,k,m,masks,actions,K) = RegionK (same variables, symmetry clause, state bound, first state 0) with at most ONE free transition: for each t in J(T) = {max(1, T-K+1), ..., T-1} a selector j_t (at most one true); the transition clause into observation t holds unless j_t; a transition whose selector is true is not a traversal (Tr counts transition t+1 out of x[t] only if j_{t+1} is false; transitions out of t with t+1 not in J always count). The transition into the LAST observation T is always constrained (lag-1 jumps are NOT covered). With J(T) empty (T <= 1) the region equals RegionK. JW contains every machine of RegionK (all selectors false), so Y1kW contains Y1k (Exact by construction).
jump_window_definition.lag_mapping: a certificate for step s is issued after T = s-1 observations; a drift4 jump at drift step d is the transition into observation d; lag L = s - d; the jump is inside J(T) iff 2 <= L <= K (Exact arithmetic).
jump_window_definition.hull: Y1kW(b, mask) = RegionK.y1k evaluated on JumpWindowRegionK with mask = mask of observation T. UNKNOWN feasibility -> every code (never certifies); y1k UNKNOWN codes count as possible (frozen tri-state semantics).
jump_window_definition.J9: brute.jumpwindow.WindowSyncLearner: brute.align.AlignedSyncLearner (SP8: SyncEventLearner rule CTR + LU-C) unchanged, plus: a certificate c that SP8 keeps (taken or counterfactual action) is kept only if Y1kW(action, mask_T) == {c} (cert_rule <SP8 path> + "+whull"), else ABSTAIN / RESYNC_AMBIGUOUS with cert_rule "whull-downgraded". Hull queries go through RegionSpace._q (memo key ("y1kW", action, mask)) so their unknowns count toward SOLVER_BUDGET. The LU-C lookahead is NOT changed (it counts what SP8 would certify, not what J9 keeps; disclosed). hull_union / hull_unknown are recorded per step while the family is supported (as J8).
jump_window_definition.not_selective_by_surprise: NEXT_ITERATION proposed applying the hull only after an unsurprising observation; the seen data had no event between drift and certificate in 28/28, so that condition would almost always hold. J9 is selective by POSITION (window excluding the last transition), not by surprise (Inferred, disclosed).

arms.SP8: brute.align.AlignedSyncLearner: the frozen SyncEventLearner(rule="CTR") (SC7 certification unchanged) with the action policy LU-C: for each action a and each code c in the support, N(a,c) = number of actions b such that, after the hypothetical full observation (a,c): family support for b is a single code s, the extended region is feasible and not saturated, the margin support for b equals s, and EITHER step t+1 is calm (no event u with (t+1) - u < W, and t+1 >= burn_in; the condition under which SC7 would certify s via "tracked-calm") OR Y1k of the extended region for b with mask {c} equals s (the LU-R condition). Score(a) = mean over c of N(a,c); ties -> passive action (as LU-R). Any solver budget hit -> 0 for that branch (as LU-R). Frozen v0.8.0 brute/align.py, run through the frozen study-010 trajectory code (experiments/brute_study_010.trajectory_2x2). Comparator.

stop_rule.cap: 2 h 00 min (7200 s) wall clock from RUN_T0 (the epoch written with the run_start_011 ledger entry); smoke, seed check, diagnostic and plan steps are outside the cap
stop_rule.streams_and_budgets: MANDATORY: 2x2 (J9, SP8, A4, A2) 4 workers 1800 s (starts at t0); gti 2 workers 2400 s (starts at t0); repro_2x2 2 workers 900 s (after 2x2); g11_2x2 2 workers 1500 s (after 2x2; mandatory sample first, then the optional rest). OPTIONAL: feas 1 worker 1200 s (starts at t0). At most 8 worker processes at once (watchdog and orchestrator not counted).
stop_rule.rate_math: before the source freeze the smoke timings are converted into a projected per-stream wall time (ledger rate_math_011, docs/research/v0.9.0/RATE_MATH_011.md); if a mandatory stream projects above 70% of its budget, the budget/worker split may be changed ONCE before the freeze as a disclosed deviation; nothing after run_start.
stop_rule.projection: at RUN_T0 + 360 s the orchestrator writes PROGRESS_011.json (cases done, rate, projected finish); reported, nothing changes.
stop_rule.watchdog: scripts/watchdog_011.py started by the operator (nohup, own session) right after RUN_T0; HEARTBEAT_011.jsonl every 2 s; at RUN_T0 + 7200 s SIGTERM to the orchestrator and every stream process group in RUN_STATE_011.json, SIGKILL after 20 s, STOP_011.json with kill wall time and latency; the orchestrator also enforces the cap itself.
stop_rule.at_cap: every unfinished stream is stopped; its checkpoint is sealed as it is (outside the cap); ledger stop_011; NO extension and NO rerun
stop_rule.scoring: every gate whose inputs are incomplete at the cap or whose mandatory stream completed after RUN_T0 + 7200 s is FAIL (reason STUDY_BUDGET)

what_counts_as_failure: any gated criterion not meeting its threshold is FAIL and is published as FAIL in GATES_011.json, README, CHANGELOG, RELEASE.json and the release notes with the same wording
GA1_011 FAIL means the window drift-and-coverage target is NOT met; a GA1_011 PASS with strict G3-prime FAIL means only lag >= 2 drift is handled
a smoke or seen-data observation never softens a FAIL
any gate with inputs incomplete at the cap, or completed after it, is FAIL (stop_rule)
a missing run_start ledger entry, a seed outside its declared range, a frozen-file hash mismatch, or a smoke run on a non-smoke seed invalidates the affected run (reported, not silently rerun)

no re-run, re-seed, threshold change or rule-constant change after the held-out run_start; reruns only for an infrastructure crash with identical code and seeds, ledgered as deviation and still inside the cap

limitations: K = 4 was chosen from seen data (exploratory lag diagnostic, disclosed); held-out seeds of this plan were never touched.
drift4 is one drift generator with jumps every 11 steps; stacked jumps (lags > 11) and other drift processes are not covered by J9.
The second implementation and the learners are by the same author.
Breadth (k > 2, s = 3) is not re-tested in v0.9.0.
Commit and ledger times are author-set.
A VM pause cannot be prevented from inside the VM; the cap counts paused time against the study (conservative).
scope_and_open: Soundness against lag-1 silent jumps with useful coverage: Open (Inferred impossible within worst-case jump semantics without vacuity; would need a probabilistic or announced-drift model)
A rate- or prior-based (probabilistic) drift model: Open
Region re-entry after a jump (second region conditioned on one jump in the last W): Open (not attempted; J9 is the hull half of it)
Stochastic worlds, learned family selection, grounding beyond templates, independent audit: Open
Cause of VM heartbeat gaps: Open
